title: The stack and priority
summary: Spells wait on the stack. Players can respond. The newest thing happens first.

checklist.label: I know spells wait on the stack
I know how to respond with an instant
I know the newest spell happens first

steps.title: The stack
steps.body:
When you cast a spell, it doesn't happen right away. It goes on the [[stack]] and waits.

While it waits, every player gets a chance to respond, for example with an [[instant]]. A response goes on top of the stack.

The stack is just a pile: the **last** thing added is the **first** to happen.

visual.altText: A pile of spells; the top one happens first.

steps.title: Priority
steps.body:
[[priority|Priority]] means it's your moment to act. Only the player with priority can cast a spell.

After a spell is cast, priority passes around the table. Each player can respond or pass.

When **all players pass in a row**, the top item on the stack [[resolve|resolves]]: it happens. Then players get priority again.

visual.altText: Priority passing between players until both pass.

steps.title: Responding with an instant
steps.body:
An example with real cards:

- You cast **Bear Cub**, a creature. It goes on the stack.
- Your opponent responds with **Cancel**, an instant that says "Counter target spell." It goes on top.
- Both of you pass. Cancel resolves first and [[counter-spell|counters]] your Bear Cub.

The Cub never reaches the battlefield. It goes to your graveyard.

visual.altText: A counterspell resolving on top of a creature spell.

check.question: Two spells are on the stack. Which one resolves first?

options.text: The one that was cast first
The one cast last, on top

check.hint: Think of a pile of plates: you take from the top.

steps.title: Why the stack matters
steps.body:
The stack lets players react. With instants you can:

- Save your creature before a removal spell resolves.
- Make your attacker bigger after your opponent has blocked.
- Cancel a big spell with a counterspell.

As a beginner, just remember: **newest first**. Instants are how you respond.

visual.altText: Three ways to use instants in response.
